column2: supersedes dec017 for the admin system, inactivity timer, build log/revert, layout files, flood/censor limits, name cleaning, session data and server console commands: g_admin.c + g_namelog.c (kernel admin, the g_admin_cmds[] table as the admin_commands sheet), g_svcmds.c (kernel svcmds), G_Layout*/G_BuildLog* (kernel layout), g_session.c (kernel session), G_ClientCleanName / ClientInactivityTimer / G_FloodLimited / G_CensorString / G_SanitiseString are ported. The host's player is the one local client (pers.localClient: never kicked, banned, ejected or dropped for inactivity) and the top admin level by default: when admin.dat has no [admin] for it, one is added at the highest defined level (5 Server Operator, ALLFLAGS). Clients get pseudo-GUIDs (LOCALHOST for the host, BOT_<NAME> for bots); bans match GUIDs only. admin.dat, layouts/<map>/<name>.dat and the g_censorship file go through a world::Fs the host implements over user:// (written) and the pk3s (read); trap_RealTime is World::real_time set by the host; trap_SendConsoleCommand(EXEC_APPEND) is World::exec, run by svcmds::run_exec with the engine lines (map, map_restart, set) handed to the host console, which is treated as a dedicated console (say/chat/a/m/cp available). Session data (restartTeam, ignore list) is kept by the host per slot across World reloads
column3: the user asked for every portable server subsystem; bots and the single human make kick/ban/mute/denybuild/putteam/lock/rename/revert meaningful, and admin.dat and layout files are user data the original already reads and writes, so the kernel only takes and returns text (D1). Without addresses or cl_guids, GUID-only bans are the faithful remainder of admin_create_ban; making the host the top admin keeps a single-player game controllable without editing admin.dat first
column4: keep dec017 (no admin at all); emulate IP addresses per bot; make every human client an admin

column2: dropped for good (dec017 stays for them): the IP/CIDR forms of ban/adjustban/showbans/namelog (G_AddressParse/G_AddressCompare, addr4parse/addr6parse, ban_matchip/namelog_matchip); unlagged (G_UnlaggedStore/Clear/Calc/On/Off/DetectCollisions): one process has no network latency, every usercmd is run at the server time it was issued, so the rewind would always be 0 ms and the code is the identity; G_ClientIsLagging: ps.ping is always 0 and its only caller, ClientConnect's duplicate-GUID check, cannot fire with the per-slot pseudo-GUIDs of dec026; vsay (bg_voice.c, Cmd_Vsay_f): neither data-1.1.0.pk3 nor the legacy assets ship voice/*.voice files, so BG_VoiceInit would load nothing; levelshot (the client's levelshot render); spec999's ping test (ps.ping is always 0, so spec999 never moves anyone). The admin and game logs are no longer dropped: dec031 supersedes that part. Additions not in the legacy C: a chat line starting with '!' runs the admin command it names (the 1.1 shrubbot g_adminParseSay convention), and layout items / build-log reverts spawn immediately instead of on the third frame, like the map structures (see spawn.rs)
column3: there are no addresses, latency or voice data in a single process; '!cmd' is how players expect to reach shrubbot commands from the chat box, and the legacy client-command path (/kick) is kept as well
column4: emulate addresses and latency; no '!' prefix

column2: bots stay command-only (dec015) and read only what a player knows: visible enemies, their own team's structures, the map (collision model, trigger entities, structure placements). BSP nav graphs are directed walk/jump/drop links (drops <=512u for aliens; humans route only over drops below MIN_FALL_DISTANCE damage), never enter trigger_hurt/target_kill volumes or lava/slime, and drop trap ledges that cannot rejoin the map's main component. Every UserCmd passes a ledge guard (no walk, strafe or jump toward a fall deeper than the class takes without heavy damage, a too-steep slope or a lethal volume, momentum and jump arc included). A link without progress for 2.5 s is blocked 30 s; a bot wedged 10 s types /kill. Dretches guard their base, evolved aliens attack in pairs, one builder per team rebuilds missing structures through build+attack, and human bots aim with more spread than aliens. Evolved aliens that do not guard raid the human base: until they are within 500u of a human structure they fight only players within 60u (what is on them), see structures at any range, and a wounded raider nearer the enemy's structures than its home presses on instead of retreating
column3: measured on the 8 maps: uncreation killed 218 bots in 10 min via its pit target_kill, nexus6/niveus left whole teams unable to reach the enemy, bots stuck up to 411 s, and dretch-only aliens never hurt a structure; these rules bring all of that inside the bots definition of done (tests/bots.rs) without giving bots any power a player lacks; with the raids, 3v3 aliens damage human structures on all 8 maps instead of 4 (atcs, karith, niveus, uncreation), which the match definition of done now requires
column4: hand-authored waypoint sheets per BSP map; teleporting stuck bots; letting bots ignore falling damage or triggers

column2: the Spreadsheet-Driven Build to-do prompt is adopted on top of the MDD: target identification is recorded in doctrine d13-d17 (decompilation not required, d10); every sheet belongs to a group in 00-groups.tsv and the book is emitted as grouped JSON (OUT_DIR/book.json, `sheetty json [group|sheet]`); a new preflight layer L8 treats every row x column intersection as needing a checkmark: placeholder markers (the PLACEHOLDERS list in crates/sheetty/src/book.rs) and non-final Status values (Todo/Stub/Partial/Blocked) are errors, so the build cannot proceed with an unfinished row (`sheetty matrix` prints the matrix)
column3: the user's process document makes completeness and grouped JSON reading mandatory; making them preflight errors enforces it mechanically instead of by review. Final statuses are Done, Verified, Replaced (a Godot equivalent) and Dropped (with a decision)
column4: a separate checklist file; warnings instead of errors

column2: impact marks, alien creep, blob shadows and wakes are mark polys clipped to the world as in the original: R_MarkFragments / R_BoxSurfaces_r / R_ChopPolyBehindPlane are ported into the trem_sim marks kernel over the BSP draw surfaces (planar faces with the lightmapVecs[2] plane, patch grids, triangle soups only with r_marksOnTriangleMeshes 1, nodraw/NOIMPACT/NOMARKS/fog surfaces skipped, only world-model surfaces in the leaves), and CG_ImpactMark / CG_AllocMark / CG_AddMarks keep MAX_MARK_POLYS 256 polys of at most 10 verts with the 10 s life and 1 s colour or alpha fade; temporary marks are rebuilt each frame. They render as one ImmediateMesh with a material per mark shader using its blendFunc (blend, add; GL_ZERO GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR, i.e. dst*(1-src) on the grey mark images, as black alpha-blended by the image's brightness, since Godot's multiply blend does not keep the destination in the Compatibility renderer) and a 0.3% pull towards the camera in view space for polygonOffset. Patch grids are the drawn tessellation (bspview's 8-step 3x3 sub-patches) instead of R_SubdividePatchToGrid, and the wake shader's tcMod/rgbGen wave animation is not reproduced
column3: Godot Decal nodes are not drawn by the Compatibility renderer the screenshots and many players use; clipping the mark like the C makes marks ordinary geometry in every renderer and keeps their shape (marks stop at ledges and do not wrap onto surfaces facing away). Using the presentation's own patch tessellation keeps marks on the curve that is actually drawn
column4: keep Decals (Forward+ only); a projector shader on the world material

column2: the server log is ported (supersedes the log part of dec027): G_LogPrintf writes g_logFile (default games.log) in the host's user folder through world::Fs::append, opened by G_InitGame and closed by G_ShutdownGame with their lines; g_logFileSync 1 writes each line, 0 buffers until the end of the frame (a log_flush system after check_votes); dedicated 1 echoes lines to the server console (G_UnEscapeString). Every G_LogPrintf of the C has its line in the same format: ClientConnect/Begin/Disconnect/Rename, ChangeTeam, Say/SayTeam/SayArea/Chat/PrivMsg/TPrivMsg, AdminMsg, AdminAuth, AdminExec (admin_log_start/admin_log/admin_log_end with ConcatArgsPrintable), CallVote/CallTeamVote/EndVote, Die, Construct, Deconstruct (G_LogDestruction), revert restore/remove, Stage, Beginning Sudden Death, Exit and the score lines of LogExit, InitGame/RealTime/ShutdownGame. pers.ip.str is empty (no addresses); G_SendGameStat builds the master-server statistics string and logs it as 'GameStat: ...' since there is no master server; BG_LoadEmoticons, SortMaps and Cmd_Test_f are ported as well
column3: a games.log is what server operators and stats tools read, and the host has file access (hostfs.rs) since dec026; the formats are checked against the C format strings in tests/log.rs
column4: keep the logs dropped; send the game stat nowhere

column2: the original main menu is the start screen: TremGame.start_in_main_menu (main.tscn as the running scene or --main-menu; +map/+devmap on the command line load a map, scenes that instance main.tscn start on the map as before), Com_Init's `cinematic splash.RoQ` plays first (cl_cin.c RoQ decoder, cinematic.rs), UI_SetActiveMenu(UIMENU_MAIN) shows ui/menus.txt, createserver's StartServer runs `map <name>` and Leave/disconnect drop the map and come back. The server browser runs on trap_LAN lists that stay empty (no network layer: localservers reaches no one, globalservers cannot resolve a master; favorites are kept in user://favorites.txt), news is the no-cURL GetNews text, demos/mods are listed but `demo`/fs_game switching are not supported. The engine cvars of the option menus live in the client store (autogen.cfg) and act on Godot (vidsnd.rs: window mode/size, gamma pass, bus volumes, max fps, texture filter, mip bias, anisotropy, MSAA, vsync); r_fullscreen defaults to the startup window state
column3: the game must start like the original (menus, intro, music, options with real effect) while staying a single-process port: every ui path is ported as far as the platform allows and the parts without a counterpart (networking, cURL, demo playback, mod switching) behave as the C does when they fail
column4: keep starting on ATCS with hud.gd's maps menu; fake a local server list; re-implement the browser in GDScript

column2: networking is ported as trem_sim kernel modules over the unchanged World (no separate crate, so the kernel allowlist, statuses.py and the compile-checked plan/impl paths keep working): huffman.rs (huffman.c), msg.rs (msg.c: bit streams, the entityState/playerState netField tables, the keyed usercmd delta), netchan.rs (net_chan.c fragments/qport/sequences + net_ip.c addresses, non-blocking std UdpSocket per source, loopback queues, NET_QueuePacket's cl/sv_packetdelay), sv.rs (sv_main/sv_client/sv_snapshot/sv_init/sv_game: connectionless getstatus/getinfo/getchallenge/connect/rcon, challenges, SV_DirectConnect, gamestate, configstrings diffed from the World each frame, PVS/area snapshots delta'd against the acked frame, rate control, timeouts, UDP downloads, master heartbeats), svgame.rs (the gentity -> entityState_t / configstring / server command mapping), cl.rs (cl_main/cl_parse/cl_input packet side/cl_cgame time: CA_* states, CL_ConnectionlessPacket, the LAN/master browser, pings, rcon), cgview.rs (cg_snapshot/cg_predict/cg_ents/cg_servercmds into a 'view World' built by World::client_view*), unlagged.rs, md5.rs and nethost.rs (Com_Frame's network half and the renderer-free engine commands). The server owns the authoritative World; every client, the listen server's own player included (loopback), renders a view World filled from snapshots, configstrings and server commands, so the presentation code reads the same fields either way. The single-process game (no network host) is untouched. Protocol 71 formats are kept bit-exact (huffman/msg/netchan checked against the original C in re/harness/net_ref.c, re/traces/net.sha256). Deviations of the server side, all in how game state becomes entityState_t: the World's event list becomes temp entities (ET_EVENTS+event, numbers from MAX_GENTITIES-3 down, 1 s reuse delay, EVENT_VALID_MSEC life; predictable playerState events carry EF_PLAYER_EVENT and are not sent to their owner, SVF_NOTSINGLECLIENT), the full event parm travels in time2, zap chains become ET_LEV2_ZAP_CHAIN entities, corpses carry their team in modelIndex2, G_TriggerMenu notices travel as 'servermenu 0 "<text>" <menu>', ClientConnect and ClientBegin run when the connect is accepted, sv_pure is 0, sv_fps is 60 to match the World's 16 ms frame (the unlagged history keeps 30 markers = the C's 500 ms), maps without vis or areas (the sheet arena) are all-visible, getchallenge always reuses the oldest slot, localservers also probes 127.0.0.1 and master names resolve on a background thread
column3: the method's tooling binds to trem_sim; keeping World authoritative and giving clients a World-shaped view keeps one presentation path for single player, listen host and remote clients, and lets the existing kernel tests and golden traces stay valid; latency and real addresses make unlagged, pings and IP bans meaningful again
column4: a separate trem_net crate with its own sheets; a GDScript or Godot ENet transport; sending World diffs instead of protocol 71 snapshots

column2: supersedes dec027 for unlagged, the IP forms and G_ClientIsLagging, and dec026's client identity rules: G_UnlaggedStore/Clear/Calc/On/Off/DetectCollisions are ported (an unlagged_store system after client_end_frame; identity in one process since every command runs at level.time); networked clients carry pers.ip from the server's userinfo 'ip' (G_AddressParse, addr4parse/addr6parse) and bans match the GUID or, without IMMUNITY, the address/CIDR (G_AddressCompare); ban/adjustban/showbans/namelog take the IP forms (ban_matchip, namelog_matchip, namelog ip[MAX_NAMELOG_ADDRS]) and the ban file keeps 'ip'; G_ClientIsLagging (ps.ping >= 999) drives ClientConnect's ghost check for a duplicate cl_guid. Remote players identify by cl_guid (32 hex digits, else 'Invalid GUID'; the client makes it as CL_UpdateGUID does: the MD5 of user://qkey, prefixed with the server address with cl_guidServerUniq 1) and are never admins by default; only the listen server's own player (ip 'localhost', pers.localClient) keeps the LOCALHOST pseudo-GUID and the top admin level of dec026; bots keep BOT_<NAME>. Banning a player without an address (host, bots) by name makes one GUID ban instead of none, and a ban's disconnect reason reaches a networked player as the C's 'disconnect' server command. g_password, sv_privateClients/sv_privatePassword and the ping limits are checked like the C
column3: with real latency and addresses these systems are what keeps play fair and servers administrable; the single-process behaviour stays identical (golden parity unchanged)
column4: keep GUID-only bans; emulate latency compensation client side

column2: supersedes the browser and createserver parts of dec032: TremGame owns a network host (nethost.rs) created by the first network command; 'map'/'devmap' start a listen server when net_enabled is set (port default 0, so +map, the default ATCS start and the console stay single-process; the createserver menu's StartServer sets net_enabled 1, as its server is meant to be joined), and connect/reconnect/localservers/globalservers/ping/serverstatus/rcon/heartbeat/serverinfo/systeminfo/killserver are engine commands of the client console and the ui. The ui's trap_LAN lists mirror the network client's (TremGame::lan_sync; LAN_UpdateVisiblePings sends the pings, favorites stay in user://favorites.txt); a dropped connection shows com_errorMessage over the main menu; UI_DrawConnectScreen's lines are drawn by the loading screen; +set and other '+' commands on the command line run at startup. The dedicated server is the pure-Rust example crates/trem_sim/examples/dedicated.rs (console on stdin, rcon, heartbeats with dedicated 2, maps from the map pk3s); a headless Godot dedicated mode is not provided. Not ported: pk3 downloads in the Godot client (the kernel's UDP download protocol is there, the host refuses a map it lacks), sv_pure checksums, demos, VoIP, cURL
column3: the original menus and console reach real servers and LAN games; keeping single process the default honours the single-player contract while one cvar (or the createserver menu) makes any map a joinable server
column4: always host a listen server like the C; a separate multiplayer menu flow

column2: client and cgame pieces ported on top of dec032: (1) the console is the original's drop-down console drawn in Rust (console.rs TremConsole: cl_console.c's scrollback ring of 78-column colour-tagged lines over the `console` shader's top half with the red line and version string, 8x16 gfx/2d/bigchars characters, Con_RunConsole's scr_conspeed slide; cl_keys.c Field_KeyDownEvent / Field_CharEvent / Console_Key with the 32-line history saved to user://q3history; common.c Field_AutoComplete with Cmd_CompleteArgument for exec, vstr, set*, toggle, reset, bind, unbind, rcon and condump), so the completion lists dropped by dec027 are ported after all (G_RegisterCommands, G_admin_register_cmds, G_ListCommands, CG_InitConsoleCommands); text without a slash is chat in a game, as in the original; (2) the name cvar (default Sys_GetCurrentUser) is the local player's userinfo: ClientConnect and CL_CheckUserinfo run ClientUserinfoChanged, and the cgame prints CG_StatusMessages' renames and team changes; (3) the joystick is legacy's raw SDL joystick (IN_JoyMove: buttons K_JOY1-16, the first hat K_JOY29-32, axes as arrow keys / K_JOY17-28 or with in_joystickUseAnalog axis events for CL_JoystickMove's j_* cvars); Godot's game-controller pad is presented in the raw order of an Xbox pad under Linux (A B X Y LB RB BACK START GUIDE LSTICK RSTICK, d-pad as hat 0, axes LX LY LT RX RY RT) and its triggers rest at 0 instead of the raw -32768; in_joystick stays 0 and there are no default joystick binds (default.cfg has none); (4) patches are tr_curve.c R_SubdividePatchToGrid grids (r_subdivisions 4) both for mark clipping and for drawing (bspview), superseding dec030's presentation tessellation; patch stitching (R_StitchAllPatches) and distance LOD are not done; (5) g_doWarmup / g_warmup gate build points, stages, spawning, averages and zaps like G_RunFrame, with SP_worldspawn's CS_WARMUP set by log::init_game (the host applies its cvars after the BSP spawns); (6) cgame debugging: testmodel / testgun / next|prevframe / next|prevskin, testPS / destroyTestPS, testTS / destroyTestTS, cgame_memory, cg_drawBBOX, cg_drawSurfNormal, cg_debugEvents, condump, clear; (7) bot balance (dec015/dec028 stay: command-only bots): human bots answer an attack on their own structures (a player sees their structures' health) for 20 s, a human builder keeps three machinegun turrets up, and bots aim at a structure with a quarter of their spread (it does not dodge); the bots definition of done adds a balance check over 6 seeds per official map (no team above 67% of a map's runs or 60% overall, mean match >= 480 s, >= 360 s per map)
column3: each is what the original client / cgame / renderer does, now that the console, gamepad and debugging commands have a place in the port; balance is checked like the rest of the bots DoD so a later change cannot tilt the matches again
column4: keep the LineEdit console; gamepad through Godot's input map; keep the tessellated patches; tune bots by hand without a check

column2: pure servers, pk3 downloads, demos, IPv6 and the headless Godot dedicated server are ported (supersedes the 'not ported' parts of dec035 except VoIP and cURL): (1) files.rs ports files.c's pure half and md4.c (FS_LoadZipFile's checksum and feed-keyed pure_checksum over the zip central directory CRCs, hashed against the original unzip.c + md4.c in re/harness/pak_ref.c, re/traces/pak.sha256; md4.c's quirk of hashing an empty block twice is kept); servers default to sv_pure 1 like the C and send sv_paks / sv_pakNames / sv_referencedPaks / sv_referencedPakNames, clients restrict their search path to the server's paks (FS_PureServerSetLoadedPaks, FS_ReorderPurePaks) and reply cp with FS_ReferencedPakPureChecksums, SV_VerifyPaks_f drops an unpure client; because Tremulous 1.1.0's data ships no qvms (they are in vms-1.1.0.pk3) and the port's cgame / ui / game are built in, a module's pak is the one holding its qvm when present, else its first data file (cgame ui/hud.txt, ui ui/menus.txt), on both sides; a server without pk3s (the sheet arena) is not pure; server ids now increase across maps (com_frameTime) so outdated cp commands are ignored; (2) downloads: CL_InitDownloads / CL_NextDownload with com_downloadPrompt (the ui's download_popmenu) and cl_allowDownload (default 0) / CL_ParseDownload writing <fs_homepath>/<name>.tmp then renaming / CL_DownloadsComplete's FS_Restart and donedl; the Godot client's fs_homepath is user:// (downloads land in user://base, rescanned into the pk3 list), the server only sends referenced paks (SV_WriteDownloadToClient); no cURL (a USE_CURL-less build); (3) demos (demo.rs): record / stoprecord / demo / timedemo / cl_timedemoLog / cl_freezeDemo / cl_autoRecordDemo with the original file format in user://demos/<name>.dm_71 (the menus' demo extension follows the protocol, 71); playback feeds CL_ParseServerMessage as cl_main.c does and the host loads the map like a connection; the single-player game stays single-process (its golden and behavioural tests depend on it), and recording it follows the original's arrangement instead: 'record' in a single-process game, or any map with cl_autoRecordDemo 1, (re)starts the map on a local server reached only through the loopback (net_enabled 0 opens no socket) and records the loopback client, so a single-player record restarts the current match; (4) IPv6: per-source ipv6 sockets bound with IPV6_V6ONLY (libc on unix), NET_OpenIP per net_enabled bits (the port's net_enabled 0, its single-process default, opens what the client default 3 would; dedicated servers default to 1 as the DEDICATED build), NET_StringToAdr's family priority (NET_PRIOV6) and connect -4/-6, [addr]:port parsing and scoped printing, NET_JoinMulticast6 when a server spawns and the LAN scan sending to NA_MULTICAST6 (net_mcast6addr / net_mcast6iface); the build container has no ipv6 so the socket tests skip there; (5) com_dedicated in Godot: godot --headless --path godot -- +set dedicated 1 (or 2) +map atcs runs TremGame with no presentation, menus or audio (hud.gd frees the ui), maps load as Worlds only, the console reads stdin (Sys_ConsoleInput on a thread), dedicated 2 heartbeats; the pure-Rust dedicated example stays
column3: the original serves and joins pure servers, fetches missing maps, records and replays demos and runs on ipv6 and as a dedicated binary; each is now possible with the network layer of dec033, and the single-process single player stays untouched by default while its recordings still come from the loopback client as in the C
column4: always run single player over the loopback (changes every single-player path and test); record single player by building snapshots from the single-process World without a client; treat the port's built-in cgame/ui as unpure (every pure server would refuse the port); keep downloads in memory and only write complete pk3s

column2: supersedes the VoIP and video parts of dec035: (1) VoIP is ported as the kernel module voip.rs over the bundled libopus 1.1 (crates/trem_opus compiles re/source/src/opus-1.1 with the cc crate using the Makefile's USE_INTERNAL_OPUS flags and object list; it cross-compiles for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu): CL_CaptureVoip (cl_voip / rate check, cl_voipUseVAD, cl_voipVADThreshold, cl_voipCaptureMult, cl_voipGainDuringCapture via S_MasterGain, 20 ms frames, up to 3 per Opus packet), CL_VoipParseTargets (all, spatial, attacker, crosshair, client numbers), CL_WritePacket's clc_voipOpus block, SV_UserVoip / SV_Voip_f / SV_WriteVoipToClient (the 64-packet queue, sv_voip, sv_voipProtocol in CS_SYSTEMINFO and getinfo's voip key, cl_voipProtocol in the userinfo), CL_ParseVoip with packet-loss concealment and generations, CL_Voip_f (ignore, unignore, gain, muteall, unmuteall; registered at the first snapshot), +voiprecord / -voiprecord and SCR_DrawVoipMeter (drawn by TremConsole). The sound system is the Godot host's: the microphone is an AudioStreamMicrophone on a VoipCapture bus whose AudioEffectCapture is read and resampled to 48 kHz mono (project.godot enables audio input), S_MasterGain scales the Master bus over s_volume, and S_RawSamples' streams are an AudioStreamGenerator player per talker (direct, at the voip gain) and an AudioStreamPlayer3D at the talker (spatial). (2) The video capture is the kernel module avi.rs (cl_avi.c byte for byte, the idx1 index kept in memory instead of the temporary .index.dat file) driven by avicap.rs: CL_Frame locks the frame time to 1000/cl_aviFrameRate (timescale applied) while recording, RE_TakeVideoFrame reads the root viewport (motion JPEG at r_aviMotionJpegQuality through Image.save_jpg_to_buffer, else bottom-up BGR lines padded to 4 bytes) and the Master bus mix is the PCM stream: Godot mixes in real time, so each video frame takes exactly S_GetSoundtime's rate/cl_aviFrameRate samples of it (silence when short, the surplus dropped). `video` keeps CL_Video_f's 'only when playing back demos' check (clc.demoplaying is ClVoip::demoplaying, for the demo player to set); TremGame.video_open is CL_OpenAVIForWriting for scripts. (3) Joystick keys reach the key catchers as cl_keys.c sends them: with the console down Console_Key (presses), with a menu open UI_KEY_EVENT (presses and releases) through TremMenus' Menu_HandleKey / Item_HandleKey, where K_JOY1-4 have no default action, bind items bind K_JOY* keys and the stick's arrow keys move the cursor; KEYCATCH_CGAME is never set by this cgame. The original menus have no VoIP options and default.cfg no +voiprecord bind, so none are added; CG_VoIPString has no engine caller in legacy
column3: voice chat, the video capture and gamepad menu control are features of the original client; porting the C with its own codec keeps the protocol 71 VoIP bytes interoperable with original clients and servers
column4: a pure-Rust Opus encoder / decoder; Godot's movie writer (--write-movie works only from the command line); emulating joystick keys as Godot input events

column2: the internet server list asks the master with the protocol number: CL_GlobalServers_f sends "getservers 71 full empty" (and "getserversExt Tremulous 71 full empty" to an ipv6 master) instead of the C's "getservers Tremulous full empty"; NET_GetPacket's ECONNRESET skip is kept on Windows (the receive loop reads on after it)
column3: the live master.tremulous.net runs darklegion's tremulous-master, which takes the first word after getservers as the protocol and filters servers on it: the C's game-name form returns an empty list (the empty online browser the user saw). Servers already advertise protocol 71 in infoResponse, so heartbeats need no change. crates/trem_sim/tests/net_master.rs runs heartbeat, getinfo check, list, ping and join against a stand-in of that master. Windows reports an ICMP port-unreachable as WSAECONNRESET on the next recvfrom; the C ignores it and so does the port
column4: keep the C's game-name request (empty list on master.tremulous.net); send both forms (duplicate entries from masters that accept both); a different master

column2: the client also speaks vanilla Tremulous 1.1.0's protocol 69 (network half; the game-data mapping is v11.rs): NetClient.protocol (71 or 69) switches every wire difference of re/source11: CL_CheckForResend's bare "getchallenge" and connect with protocol 69, challengeResponse / connectResponse without the client challenge (NET_CompareBaseAdr), Netchan::protocol 69 headers without the challenge checksum, CL_Netchan_Encode / CL_Netchan_Decode, 1.1's entityStateFields (no weaponAnim, powerups in the misc slot, generic1 8 bits) and playerStateFields (PlayerState11 with ammo / powerups arrays), MSG_ReadString's '%' translation, Com_HashKey usercmd keys, no VoIP; the 1.1 states stay the delta bases (ClSnapshot.ps11, entity_baselines11, parse_entities11, configstrings11) while the cgame gets v11::ps_from_11 / es_from_11 / configstring_from_11 (also for "cs" commands) / server_command_from_11 (extra commands queued for take_pending_server_command); outgoing usercmds go through usercmd_to_11 and every reliable command except the engine's own (disconnect, cp, vdr, download, nextdl, stopdl, donedl) through client_command_to_11. Network modes: cl_netProtocol (archived) 0 Auto / 71 / 69; Auto sends "getinfo xxx" first and takes the infoResponse's protocol (69 vanilla, else legacy), legacy after PROTOCOL_PROBE_TIME (1 s) without an answer; the loopback is always legacy; connect [-4|-6] server [-1|-69|-71] forces one (-1 is GrangerHub 1.3's flag for 1.1 servers). The browser asks every master for "getservers 71 ..." and "getservers 69 ..." and merges the answers (duplicates dropped, CL_GSRSequenceInformation's resets skipped while merging); CL_ServerInfoPacket takes protocol 69 infoResponses without gamename and 71 ones with gamename Tremulous; serverInfo_t carries the protocol; the Godot browser shows it in the Game Type column ("base 1.1" / "base 1.3"), filters on ui_browserProtocol (joinserver.menu: a "Version:" All / 1.3 / 1.1 multi in the top half of the legend's slot, the legend at .2 below it) and joins with "connect <addr> -<protocol>"; options.menu gets "Server Protocol:" Auto / 1.3 (71) / 1.1 (69) (H grows by one row); both repacked with pack_assets.py. Demos of a protocol 69 connection are not recorded
column3: vanilla 1.1.0 servers are still the majority of the live list; the original 1.3 engine (GrangerHub) joins them through alternateProtocol 2 branches of the same files, which is the guide here, while re/source11's own C is the authority. The wire is byte-checked: crates/trem_sim/tests/net_v11.rs hashes the port's 1.1 deltas, keys, coders and netchan packets against re/harness/msg69_ref.c (re/source11 msg.c / huffman.c / net_chan.c compiled natively with cl_net_chan.c's coders copied verbatim; re/traces/msg69.sha256) and runs a real 1.1.0 tremded end to end (join, team humans, class rifle, walk, pure cp with a stand-in vms pak, a UDP download, disconnect), skipping without the binary. darklegion's master filters by protocol and does not say which query a list answers, so the lists are merged and each server's own infoResponse names its protocol
column4: a separate 1.1 client (two network stacks); GrangerHub's per-protocol master addresses and ports (the live master serves both protocols on one port); asking the master for 69 only in the vanilla mode (the browser could not show both); recording 1.1 demos with the legacy extension

column2: the game-data half of the Tremulous 1.1.0 (protocol 69) client: (1) the 1.1.0 tables are sheets synthesised from the ORIGINAL 1.1.0 code (re/harness/v11_ref: bg_misc.c's BG_Find* after BG_InitClassOverrides / BG_InitBuildableOverrides with data-1.1.0.pk3's overrides/ kept in re/source11/assets; re/harness/consts11: every define and enum member of the 1.1.0 headers evaluated by the compiler; dumps in re/traces/v11, re/harness/synth_v11.py writes classes11 / weapons11 / upgrades11 / buildables11 / constants11 and the Event11 / MeansOfDeath11 / EntityType11 / Stat11 / Pers11 / Menu11 / PmType11 / Ability11 domains); each 1.1 row names its legacy row (`legacy`), and 1.1's hovel (BA_A_HOVEL) and advanced construction kit (WP_HBUILD2) are presentation-only legacy rows (buildables `hovel` num 16, weapons `ackit` num 27) with no stage (the stages column of weapons/buildables is now optional), so no legacy server allows them and the BSP spawn / entity-name lookups skip stageless rows, while the presentation draws them from the player's data-1.1.0.pk3 like any structure or weapon; (2) kernel/v11.rs maps every 1.1 number and encoding to legacy (weapons, upgrades, classes, buildables, EV_*, MOD_*, ET_*, eFlags, pm_flags, pm_type, STAT_*/PERS_* layout incl. the packed ammo, alien frags as credits, the pounce / trample / lcannon charges rescaled, the structures' 5-bit health and toggle bits, corpses, temp event entities re-encoded as the port's event entities, configstrings incl. team votes and the 1.1-only CS_BUILDPOINTS / CS_STAGES / CS_SPAWNS / CS_SCORES past legacy's CS_MAX, server commands chat / tchat / scores / tinfo / servermenu (as the port's notice texts) / print (the winner as CS_WINNER), client commands and usercmd buttons); the 1.1 playerState words legacy has no room for travel in legacy ps.misc[] so ps_to_11 inverts ps_from_11; (3) kernel/pmove11.rs is 1.1.0's bg_pmove.c + bg_slidemove.c on the 1.1 playerState (with 1.1's q_math.c VectorNormalize, which rounds differently, and its [180, 540) view angles), byte-exact against re/harness/pmove11_ref (the 1.1.0 bg code linked with the shared legacy collision) over sheets/domain/scenarios11.tsv, re/traces/arena11.sha256; the cgame predicts with it when Cgame::vanilla is set, uses 1.1's class / structure boxes and also fires the events 1.1 carries on regular entities; (4) the menus and HUD of a vanilla World show 1.1.0 ui_main.c's lists and the 1.1 prices / frag costs / build points
column3: a 1.1.0 server runs 1.1's movement, numbering and balance: a client predicting legacy movement rubber-bands (tests/net_v11.rs: 126 prediction misses against 0) and legacy numbers would draw the wrong weapons and structures; data from sheets keeps the 1.1 values checked against the original program like the legacy ones
column4: translate 1.1 states into legacy pmove inputs (legacy movement differs in sprint, stamina, landing, walljump and pounce); a separate 1.1 cgame (duplicates the whole client); full legacy rows for the hovel and the advanced kit (the legacy server would offer them); keep the raw 1.1 playerState beside the legacy one in the snapshot (the network layer's structure)

column2: the server browser works in the Godot client: (1) the client's AS_* source numbers are q_shared.h's (AS_GLOBAL 0, AS_MPLAYER 1, AS_LOCAL 2, AS_FAVORITES 3), shared with the ui as in the C; (2) the disconnected client still runs CL_Frame's network part every frame (the browser's answers are read there); (3) LAN_MarkServerVisible(source, -1) marks the slots of servers that answer later too, as the C's fixed arrays do; (4) the LAN scan waits its whole second before it ends; (5) a server on this machine answering both the loopback copy of the scan (dec033) and the broadcast is listed once
column3: (1)-(3) are the C's behaviour the port had lost: the cl.rs numbering (LOCAL 0, GLOBAL 1, FAVORITES 2) sent the ui's ping requests to the wrong list, so the Internet and LAN lists never got pings and stayed empty, and nothing read the answers while disconnected; (4) the port's servers answer at their next frame, up to 50 ms after a tremded would, and the C ends the scan at the first answer; (5) the loopback copies are the port's own addition. godot/tests/lan_browser_shot.gd shows a 1.1.0 tremded and a port server listed with their versions and the Version filter
column4: keep the cl.rs numbering and translate in lan_sync; pump the network only while the browser menu is open

column2: map surfaces are drawn from the full shader script, stage by stage (q3shader.rs, bspview.rs plan_passes): (1) every stage of a surface's shader is a pass (Godot next_pass) with its own blend, rgbGen / alphaGen (const, wave incl. noise, vertex, exactVertex, lightingSpecular ...), tcGen (lightmap, environment, vector), tcMods (scale, scroll, rotate, turb, stretch, transform), animMap, alphaFunc and clampMap; deformVertexes (wave, bulge, move, autosprite, autosprite2) move every pass alike; (2) a light map + texture pair, or a lone opaque texture stage, stays the base pass the enhanced mode lights, and a last $lightmap filter over blended stages is folded into the passes before it; (3) GL blend pairs map onto Godot's mix / add / premul / mul with the stage's output adjusted (e.g. GL_DST_COLOR GL_SRC_ALPHA = mul by rgb + a), the x2 overbright applied to what a stage adds and not to a multiply; (4) a pass over an earlier one (depthFunc equal) and polygonOffset decals are pulled towards the camera in view space; transparent passes are ordered by the shader's sort, then stage; (5) skies draw the box and the cloud layers at cloudheight (R_InitSkyTexCoords) with their tcMods and blends, the box at identityLight; (6) the vanilla mode fogs through fog brushes with a screen pass (alpha = sqrt(distance in fog / distanceToOpaque)); the enhanced mode keeps its volumetric fog
column3: the minimal reader drew one image per surface: light fixtures lost their glow layer, pulsing / flickering lights stood still, glass came out at full brightness, force fields / slime / sky clouds did not move, Uncreation's cloud-only sky was a flat colour, arachnid2 / transit had no fog without the enhanced mode, and transit's decals z-fought (flickered) with their walls
column4: bake each shader into one Godot material per surface (no exact blend chain); a texture atlas for animMap (bleeding at the frame seams)

column2: the enhanced mode's dynamic shadows are world-fixed (lamps.rs): at map load the light grid's directions (every cell, weighted by its directed light) are clustered into 12 directions, the sky's q3map_sun kept exact as one; up to 6 shadow-only directional lights (negative energy; Godot draws at most 8) stand along the directions that light the area around the view (picked 4 times a second, faded in / out, never turned); a surface takes a light's shadow only where its own grid direction is within ~30 degrees of the light's (smoothstep 0.80-0.90), taking the directed share of its baked light away; the map's own shadows stay its light maps; 12 directions fit 82-99% of the shipped maps' light, 70-98% near the view has its shadow light
column3: the one shadow sun turned to the grid direction at the camera, so every shadow swung as the viewer walked; compiled maps keep no light entities and the q3map_surfacelight lamps explain under a third of atcs's light, so the lamps cannot be rebuilt; the grid knows every spot's light
column4: point lights at estimated lamps (grid ray voting did not converge: entity lights were stripped, directions are blends); the light grid direction per caster (no per-caster light in Godot); re-lighting the map in real time from guessed lamps (would not match the maps' look)

column2: the LAN scan also sends getinfo to each local network's own broadcast address (a /24 per local IPv4 address: getifaddrs on unix, the host name's addresses on Windows) besides 255.255.255.255 and the ipv6 group; a listen / dedicated server prints the addresses LAN players join at and, on Windows, the firewall hint
column3: Windows sends the all-ones broadcast out of one adapter only (the best route: a VPN or virtual-machine adapter can take it), so a friend's scan never reached the host on the real network
column4: the C's 255.255.255.255 only (the bug); interface netmasks via GetAdaptersAddresses (a large FFI for home networks that are /24)

column2: a network server (listen or dedicated) asks the router to forward its UDP port (UPnP IGD: SSDP discovery, AddPortMapping with a permanent lease, a day when refused, GetExternalIPAddress; upnp.rs, net_upnp 0 turns it off) on a thread, prints the address internet players join at (or why they cannot: no UPnP router, a private / CGNAT router address) on the host's console, and takes the mapping back when the server stops; the 4K texture and sound packs are looked for beside the executable first (a packaged game ships them), then in user://
column3: a friend joining over the internet reached the host's router, which forwarded nothing: the join timed out; a packaged game on another PC had no user:// packs
column4: manual port forwarding only (most players cannot); NAT punch-through through a master (needs a service and both ends patched)

column2: on Windows a listen server checks, on a thread and read only (PowerShell Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter / Get-NetFirewallRule / Get-NetConnectionProfile), whether an enabled inbound allow rule for the running exe covers every connected network category (a block rule wins); if not it tells the host on the console, and the client command firewall_allow asks Windows (netsh through its own administrator prompt) to add a UDP allow rule for this exe on the missing categories (firewall.rs)
column3: the LAN self-test passes on one PC because traffic to its own address is not filtered, while the exported Tremulous.exe has no inbound allow rule, so a friend on the same Wi-Fi saw no server and could not join; vanilla never checked and left this to the OS prompt
column4: only the generic hint of dec045 (the player cannot tell whether it applies); an installer that adds the rule (none yet); adding the rule silently (needs admin and changes the OS without asking)

column2: the networked cgame's view World keeps an entity's owner only for missiles (their otherEntityNum); every other snapshot entity gets ENTITYNUM_NONE, so World::trace, which skips entities owned by the mover or the mover's owner (SV_ClipMoveToEntities), no longer skips structures and players whose otherEntityNum is 0 or the local client: CG_ClipMoveToEntities skips nothing but skipNumber (tests/net_predict_solid.rs)
column3: online the predicted player walked through turrets and other structures and the server pulled him back (rubber band); the owner asked to collide with them
column4: a separate CG-only trace in cgview (duplicates World::trace); skip by owner only in the server world (same effect, wider change)

column2: the port binds k to voip_toggle (a client command that flips cl_voipSend like a +voiprecord that stays down and prints 'VoIP: microphone on/off'); configs written before it get the bind once on startup if k is free (port_bindsVersion, archived; PORT_LATER_BINDS)
column3: the owner asked for a key that toggles the microphone, not v (third person) and not push-to-talk; k is free in default.cfg and the port's additions and is the voice key in other shooters
column4: toggle cl_voipSend on the key (no feedback); only a fresh config gets the bind (existing players would never see it)

column2: voice chat in the port's terms: voip_toggle keeps its own state (Client.voip_toggle) because CL_CaptureVoip sets cl_voipSend back to 0 when it will not capture, and the kernel now records why (ClVoip.refused: not in a game, the server has no voice chat, a demo, cl_voip 0, cl_voipCaptureMult 0), which turns the toggle off with that reason on the console and the HUD; outside an online game the toggle goes off at once; a voice HUD (voiphud.rs, cl_voipHud 1, archived) drawn by TremConsole over the game: MIC ON / TALKING with the capture level, MIC OFF and refusal notes for 3 s, and the players heard in the last 400 ms; with it on, SCR_DrawVoipMeter's line is not drawn; the options' Sound panel gets a Voice Chat... button (a copy of the Doppler row) to a port page (ui/port_voice.menu, built at load) with Voice Chat (cl_voip), Microphone (s_voipInputDevice, archived: AudioServer.input_device by name, the devices AudioServer lists when the menus load), Mic Volume (cl_voipCaptureMult), Sound While Talking (cl_voipGainDuringCapture), Voice Activation (cl_voipUseVAD) and Voice HUD; the port pages' rows now use the legacy menudef.h numbers the menus are read with (YESNO 14, MULTI 15: the enhanced-audio page had 1.1.0's 11 / 12, an ownerdraw and a numeric field) and cvarStrList entries are comma separated (adjacent strings concatenate in Parse_ReadToken)
column3: the owner: the toggle printed on every press (on a server without VoIP, which reset the cvar), and asked for a HUD showing talking and the toggle state, and a microphone setting
column4: keep the kernel's silent reset (the C's behaviour, but the key then seems broken); an in-game Godot UI for the settings (the menus are the original's menu scripts)

column2: at startup (not only when hosting: the LAN scan's answers from other PCs need the inbound rule too) the game runs the dec047 firewall check; when other PCs cannot reach it (no allow rule, or a block rule) Windows' own dialog (DisplayServer.dialog_show) asks once a run: Allow runs, on a thread, an elevated PowerShell (Start-Process -Verb RunAs, the script as -EncodedCommand) that removes this exe's inbound block rules and adds the UDP allow rule for the networks found lacking one, then checks again; Not now; Don't ask again sets net_firewallPrompt 0 (archived); firewall_allow does the same as Allow
column3: the owner: LAN failed until the firewall was set by hand; asked for a Windows popup that asks to allow the game
column4: rely on Windows' own allow-access prompt (it appears once per exe path, and Cancel leaves a block rule that wins over any allow); an installer (not yet)

column2: the 4K pack's files shrink losslessly (crates/trem_hdpack): TREMHD02 keeps the 40-byte header and stores each mip level as one zstd frame (level 19) after a table of their sizes, so the larger levels can still be skipped (r_hdMaxSize) and every level decompresses to exactly the TREMHD01 bytes the GPU took before; byte-identical textures become TREMHDLN links to the first of them (one hop, a pack-relative path, never '..'); the game reads 01, 02 and links, the builder writes 02, and hdpack pack converts an existing pack, reading every new file back through the game's reader before it replaces the old one (written beside it, renamed)
column3: the owner asked to make the game smaller without lowering texture quality; the pack was 10.65 GB of the 10.9 GB release; measured on the whole pack: 289 duplicates (1.82 GB) became links and zstd 19 kept 31.3 % of the rest, 10.651 GB -> 2.762 GB, read at the speed of the uncompressed files (about 340 MB/s on a sample)
column4: 2K textures or per-map packs (lower quality or less content); recompressing to BC7 / RDO-tuned blocks (lossy); one zstd frame per file (no level skipping)

column2: the voice chat fixes after the owner's test (godot/tests/voice_shot.tscn, the owner's own settings): the menus' copy of the cvars (UI_UpdateCvars' list) now includes the voice cvars, so the page shows their values (it showed No / blank); the port pages place text the legacy ui_shared.c way (right-aligned labels end at x + w + textalignx: -150 for the 300-wide rows; title, note and buttons centred with textalignx 0 and textvalign 1; title and note typed ITEM_TYPE_TEXT, else they are not drawn) and open at x 240 beside the options window instead of over it; the Sound panel's Enhanced Audio... and Voice Chat... buttons are that panel's own rows (OpenAL, Doppler + 1) turned into buttons, so they sit in its label column; with voice activation (cl_voipUseVAD 1) the K toggle gates it (the capture host reads cl_voipUseVAD as 0 while the toggle is off), since CL_CaptureVoip otherwise keeps cl_voipSend at 1 and K could not close the microphone; the voice HUD is drawn at 10 units from y 190 on the left (it was 8 units at y 300, over the tutorial lines)
column3: the owner: no voice HUD, and the voice settings looked glitched (screenshots: rows outside the page, wrong values, the page over the options)
column4: a Godot-side settings dialog (the menus are the original's menu scripts); voice activation ignoring the toggle (the C's behaviour)

column2: downloaded pak names are validated before anything is fetched or written: a name from the server must be a relative "<dir>/<name>.pk3" made of [A-Za-z0-9_.+-] and "/" (at most 128 characters; no empty, dot-leading or dot-ending component; no Windows device name), checked when the download list is built, again when the list is used, and again where the path is made (all path components plain names). The pak is written to <name>.pk3.tmp, its checksum is verified before it takes its final name, and the file is deleted if the checksum does not match, the transfer fails or the connection ends first
column3: the client built the destination from whatever name the server listed, with only the original engine's "../" test; the original engine meant to keep downloads to plain .pk3 names inside the game folder, and a file that failed the checksum stayed on disk. Existing names (slacker/vms-1.1.0-bunker_220207-144309.pk3, gpp/*.pk3) are unchanged
column4: rewriting a bad name into a good one (silently changes what is asked of the server); keeping only the "../" test; refusing downloads altogether
